OLDCASEPICS.Acute Cholecystitis: Imaging clue 1: Ultrasound (Gallstones with a thick wall and fluid around the gallbladder: acute cholecystitis)
OLDCASEPICS.Acute Gout: Tests clue 1: Microscopy (Needle-shaped, negatively birefringent crystals: gout)
OLDCASEPICS.Acute Pericarditis: Tests clue 1: 12-lead ECG (Widespread concave ST elevation with PR depression: pericarditis)
OLDCASEPICS.Acute Pulmonary Oedema: Imaging clue 1: X-ray (Pulmonary oedema: big heart, bat-wing shadowing, effusions)
OLDCASEPICS.Acute Pyelonephritis: Tests clue 1: Microscopy (White cell casts: infection or inflammation in the kidney itself)
OLDCASEPICS.Atrial Fibrillation with Fast Ventricula: Tests clue 1: 12-lead ECG (Irregularly irregular with no P waves: AF with a fast rate)
OLDCASEPICS.Atrial Flutter: Tests clue 1: 12-lead ECG (Atrial flutter with 2:1 block: sawtooth waves at 300 a minute)
OLDCASEPICS.Biliary Colic: Imaging clue 1: Ultrasound (Gallstones with a normal, thin wall: biliary colic)
OLDCASEPICS.COPD Exacerbation: Tests clue 1: Blood gas (Acute-on-chronic respiratory acidosis (raised bicarbonate))
OLDCASEPICS.Community-Acquired Pneumonia:
Tests clue 2: Microscopy (Gram-positive lancet-shaped diplococci)
Imaging clue 1: X-ray (Right lower lobe consolidation with air bronchograms)
OLDCASEPICS.Complete Heart Block: Tests clue 1: 12-lead ECG (Complete heart block: P waves and QRS complexes dissociated)
OLDCASEPICS.Deep Vein Thrombosis: Imaging clue 1: Ultrasound (Vein does not compress and has echoes inside: deep vein thrombosis)
OLDCASEPICS.Diabetic Ketoacidosis: Tests clue 2: Blood gas (High anion gap metabolic acidosis with respiratory compensation)
OLDCASEPICS.Hyperosmolar Hyperglycaemic State: Tests clue 2: Lab panel (Very high glucose and osmolality without ketoacidosis: hyperosmolar hyperglycaemic state)
OLDCASEPICS.Non-ST-Elevation Myocardial Infarction: Tests clue 1: 12-lead ECG (Lateral ST depression and T-wave inversion: ischaemia (NSTEMI))
OLDCASEPICS.Opioid Overdose: Tests clue 1: Blood gas (Acute respiratory acidosis from hypoventilation)
OLDCASEPICS.Panic Attack: Tests clue 2: Blood gas (Acute respiratory alkalosis)
OLDCASEPICS.Primary Spontaneous Pneumothorax: Imaging clue 1: X-ray (Left pneumothorax: a visible lung edge with no markings beyond it)
OLDCASEPICS.Pulmonary Embolism: Tests clue 2: 12-lead ECG (Sinus tachycardia, S1Q3T3, right heart strain: think PE)
OLDCASEPICS.ST-Elevation Myocardial Infarction: Tests clue 1: 12-lead ECG (Anterior ST elevation in V1–V4: anterior STEMI)
OLDCASEPICS.Sickle Cell Pain Crisis: Tests clue 1: Microscopy (Sickle cells with target cells and Howell–Jolly bodies)
OLDCASEPICS.Small Bowel Obstruction: Imaging clue 1: X-ray (Dilated central small-bowel loops with valvulae conniventes)
OLDCASEPICS.Supraventricular Tachycardia: Tests clue 1: 12-lead ECG (Regular narrow-complex tachycardia with no visible P waves: SVT (AVNRT))
OLDCASEPICS.Accidental Hypothermia: Tests clue 1: 12-lead ECG (Bradycardia with J (Osborn) waves: hypothermia)
OLDCASEPICS.Acute Post-Streptococcal Glomerulonephri: Tests clue 1: Microscopy (Red cell casts: bleeding from the glomerulus)
OLDCASEPICS.Cardiac Tamponade:
Tests clue 1: 12-lead ECG (Low voltage with electrical alternans: think tamponade)
Imaging clue 1: Ultrasound (Large pericardial effusion with right ventricular collapse: tamponade)
OLDCASEPICS.Giant Cell Arteritis: Imaging clue 1: Ultrasound (Dark halo around the temporal artery: giant cell arteritis)
OLDCASEPICS.Hydatidiform Mole: Imaging clue 1: Ultrasound ("Snowstorm" uterus with no fetus: complete hydatidiform mole)
OLDCASEPICS.Hypercalcaemia of Malignancy: Tests clue 2: 12-lead ECG (Short QT interval: hypercalcaemia)
OLDCASEPICS.Hyperkalaemia: Tests clue 2: 12-lead ECG (Tall peaked T waves, wide QRS, flat P waves: hyperkalaemia)
OLDCASEPICS.Hypertrophic Pyloric Stenosis: Imaging clue 1: Ultrasound (Thick, long pyloric muscle: hypertrophic pyloric stenosis)
OLDCASEPICS.Meningococcal Meningitis: Tests clue 2: Microscopy (Gram-negative diplococci inside neutrophils)
OLDCASEPICS.Penetrating Abdominal Trauma: Imaging clue 1: Ultrasound (Free fluid around the spleen: a positive FAST)
OLDCASEPICS.Perforated Peptic Ulcer: Imaging clue 1: X-ray (Free gas under the right hemidiaphragm (pneumoperitoneum))
OLDCASEPICS.Pulmonary Tuberculosis:
Tests clue 1: Microscopy (Acid-fast bacilli: red rods on a blue background)
Imaging clue 1: X-ray (Right upper lobe cavity)
OLDCASEPICS.Rhabdomyolysis: Tests clue 2: Lab panel (Dipstick blood with no red cells on microscopy: myoglobinuria)
OLDCASEPICS.Ruptured Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm: Imaging clue 1: Ultrasound (Abdominal aortic aneurysm with mural thrombus)
OLDCASEPICS.Ruptured Ectopic Pregnancy: Imaging clue 1: Ultrasound (Empty uterus with free fluid in the pelvis: ruptured ectopic until proven otherwise)
OLDCASEPICS.Salicylate Overdose: Tests clue 1: Blood gas (Respiratory alkalosis plus a high anion gap metabolic acidosis: think salicylate)
OLDCASEPICS.Severe Aortic Stenosis: Tests clue 1: 12-lead ECG (Left ventricular hypertrophy with strain)
OLDCASEPICS.Subarachnoid Haemorrhage: Tests clue 2: 12-lead ECG (Giant, deep T-wave inversion with a long QT: cerebral T waves)
OLDCASEPICS.Tension Pneumothorax: Imaging clue 1: Ultrasound (Barcode (stratosphere) sign: no lung sliding, pneumothorax)
OLDCASEPICS.Testicular Torsion: Imaging clue 1: Ultrasound (No colour flow in an enlarged left testis: testicular torsion)
OLDCASEPICS.Thyroid Storm: Tests clue 2: 12-lead ECG (Irregularly irregular with no P waves: AF with a fast rate)
OLDCASEPICS.Tricyclic Antidepressant Overdose: Tests clue 1: 12-lead ECG (Sinus tachycardia, broad QRS and a tall terminal R in aVR: sodium-channel blockade)
OLDCASEPICS.Ventricular Tachycardia: Tests clue 1: 12-lead ECG (Broad-complex tachycardia with AV dissociation: ventricular tachycardia)
OLDCASEPICS.Wellens Syndrome: Tests clue 1: 12-lead ECG (Deep symmetrical T inversion in V2–V3: Wellens (critical LAD))
OLDCASEPICS.Acute Lymphoblastic Leukaemia: Tests clue 2: Microscopy (Many blasts with scanty cytoplasm and no Auer rods: acute lymphoblastic leukaemia)
OLDCASEPICS.Acute Rheumatic Fever: Tests clue 2: 12-lead ECG (First-degree AV block: PR interval over 200 ms)
OLDCASEPICS.Addisonian Crisis: Tests clue 1: Lab panel (Low sodium with high potassium: think adrenal insufficiency)
OLDCASEPICS.Cerebral Malaria: Tests clue 1: Microscopy (Ring forms inside red cells, some doubled: P. falciparum)
OLDCASEPICS.Cholera:
Tests clue 1: Blood gas (Normal anion gap metabolic acidosis with hypokalaemia)
Tests clue 2: Microscopy (Darting comma-shaped bacteria (Vibrio))
OLDCASEPICS.Cryptococcal Meningitis: Tests clue 2: Microscopy (Encapsulated budding yeasts with clear halos: Cryptococcus)
OLDCASEPICS.Digoxin Toxicity: Tests clue 2: 12-lead ECG (Slow AF with scooped "reverse tick" ST depression: digoxin effect)
OLDCASEPICS.Ethylene Glycol Poisoning: Tests clue 2: Microscopy (Envelope-shaped calcium oxalate crystals)
OLDCASEPICS.Falciparum Malaria: Tests clue 1: Microscopy (Ring forms inside red cells, some doubled: P. falciparum)
OLDCASEPICS.Guillain–Barré Syndrome: Tests clue 1: Lab panel (High protein with a normal cell count (albuminocytological dissociation): Guillain–Barré)
OLDCASEPICS.HELLP Syndrome: Tests clue 2: Microscopy (Schistocytes (fragmented red cells) with very few platelets)
OLDCASEPICS.HSV Encephalitis: Tests clue 1: Lab panel (Lymphocytes and red cells with a normal glucose: viral encephalitis, think HSV)
OLDCASEPICS.Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy: Tests clue 1: 12-lead ECG (Very large voltages with deep T-wave inversion: hypertrophic cardiomyopathy)
OLDCASEPICS.Methanol Poisoning: Tests clue 1: Blood gas (High anion gap acidosis with a raised osmolal gap: toxic alcohol)
OLDCASEPICS.Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension Crisis: Tests clue 2: 12-lead ECG (Right axis deviation with right ventricular strain)
OLDCASEPICS.Splenic Rupture: Imaging clue 1: Ultrasound (Free fluid around the spleen: a positive FAST)
OLDCASEPICS.Thrombotic Thrombocytopenic Purpura: Tests clue 1: Microscopy (Schistocytes (fragmented red cells) with very few platelets)
OLDCASEPICS.Torsades de Pointes: Tests clue 1: 12-lead ECG (Long QT, then polymorphic VT twisting around the baseline: torsades de pointes)
OLDCASEPICS.Tumour Lysis Syndrome: Tests clue 1: Lab panel (High potassium, phosphate and urate with low calcium: tumour lysis syndrome)
OLDCASEPICS.Amoebic Liver Abscess: Imaging clue 1: Ultrasound (Single large dark lesion in the liver: liver abscess)
OLDCASEPICS.Brugada Syndrome: Tests clue 1: 12-lead ECG (Coved ST elevation in V1–V2 with T inversion: Brugada type 1)
OLDCASEPICS.Diphtheria: Tests clue 2: 12-lead ECG (First-degree AV block: PR interval over 200 ms)
OLDCASEPICS.Lead Poisoning: Tests clue 1: Microscopy (Small pale red cells with basophilic stippling: think lead)
OLDCASEPICS.Lyme Carditis: Tests clue 1: 12-lead ECG (Complete heart block: P waves and QRS complexes dissociated)
OLDCASEPICS.Methaemoglobinaemia: Tests clue 1: Blood gas (Normal pO₂ with a saturation gap: methaemoglobinaemia)
OLDCASEPICS.Thyrotoxic Periodic Paralysis: Imaging clue 1: 12-lead ECG (Flat T waves and prominent U waves: hypokalaemia)
OLDCASEPICS.Tuberculous Meningitis: Tests clue 1: Lab panel (Lymphocytes, very high protein and very low glucose: tuberculous meningitis)
OLDCASEPICS.African Trypanosomiasis: Tests clue 1: Microscopy (Trypanosomes: wavy flagellated parasites between red cells)
OLDCASEPICS.Grayanotoxin (Mad Honey) Poisoning: Tests clue 1: 12-lead ECG (Second-degree AV block, Mobitz I (Wenckebach))
OLDCASEPICS.Inhalational Anthrax:
Tests clue 1: Microscopy (Large gram-positive rods in chains ("boxcars"))
Imaging clue 1: X-ray (Widened mediastinum with pleural effusions)
OLDCASEPICS.Primary Amoebic Meningoencephalitis: Tests clue 2: Microscopy (Motile amoebic trophozoites in CSF: Naegleria fowleri)
OLDCASEPICS.Visceral Leishmaniasis: Tests clue 2: Microscopy (Macrophage packed with Leishman–Donovan bodies)

NOTES.gbs: Only the protein (180 mg/dL) and the normal cell count come from the case. The other CSF values are mine.
NOTES.tbm: Lymphocytes, protein 320 mg/dL and a very low glucose come from the case. The cell count, glucose value, ADA and opening pressure are mine.
NOTES.hsvcsf: The case says lymphocytes, red cells, raised protein and normal glucose. All the numbers, including the tube 1 and tube 3 red cell counts, are mine.
NOTES.addison: Na 124 and K 6.1 come from the case. Chloride, bicarbonate, urea and creatinine are mine.
NOTES.tls: K, phosphate, urate and calcium come from the case. LDH and CK are mine (CK is there to rule out rhabdomyolysis).
NOTES.rhabdo: Blood 3+ with no red cells comes from the case. Colour, protein and casts are mine.
NOTES.hhs: Glucose, osmolality, ketones, pH and bicarbonate come from the case. Sodium and urea are mine.
NOTES.salicylate: Every value is mine. The case only says respiratory alkalosis plus a high anion gap acidosis.
NOTES.af: Drawn at about 148/min. Now also used for Thyroid Storm, whose report says AF at 164.
NOTES.firstdeg: Drawn at 64/min with a PR of about 340 ms, and used for both Acute Rheumatic Fever and Diphtheria.
NOTES.chb: Existing Lyme carditis picture, now also used for Complete Heart Block.
NOTES.schisto: Existing TTP picture, now also used for HELLP. The explanation mentions TTP.
NOTES.malaria: Existing thin-film picture, now also used for Cerebral Malaria, whose report says thick film.
NOTES.lungm: The case report says "absent lung sliding"; the picture shows the M-mode barcode sign.
NOTES.cerebralt: Drawn widespread with a long QT; the case report says "deep symmetrical T-wave inversion".
NOTES.tamp: Second picture for Cardiac Tamponade, on top of the existing electrical alternans ECG.

PREV.Acute Asthma Exacerbation: Good, maybe include details that the patient is in tripod position
PREV.Acute Pericarditis: Should not send home someone with a cardiac problem confirmed, risk of tamponade
PREV.Atrial Flutter: Good, but the ECG doesn't really show the flutter well, maybe make it a 3:1 so it views better?
PREV.Community-Acquired Pneumonia: Good, but rusty sputum might conflict with Tuberculosis no?
PREV.Ischaemic Stroke: Maybe vary right and right stroke
PREV.Peritonsillar Abscess: Good, maybe need urgent theatre since it is a threatening airway diseases (risk of obstruction)
PREV.Pulmonary Embolism: Good, but I think PE should go to ICU (high risk of deterioration)
PREV.Scaphoid Fracture: Good, maybe add with orthopedic follow-up visit
PREV.Severe Pre-eclampsia: Severe PE should require ICU since it can develop into PE
PREV.Supraventricular Tachycardia: Shouldn't send someone home with SVT until cardiac causes are excluded, admitted to at least a ward and ICU if unstable haemodynamically
PREV.Transient Ischaemic Attack: Good, MRI or MRA would help. DSA as well
PREV.antstemi: ST elevation looks good, on V1, but on V2-3 looks weird since the one elevated is not the ST by itself but the RST (still going up an R wave, maybe fix that)
PREV.hyperk: Okay, maybe add more severe form like sine wave?
PREV.s1q3t3: The S in lead 1 is not deep enough, Q should be deeper aswelll.
PREV.flutter: flutter should mimic sawtooth more, maybe at a 3:1 or 2:1 but better P visualization, since I do get that its flutter but there's only 1 p before each QRS
PREV.hypok: P is missing, should be T, U then another P? Crosscheck.
PREV.dka: Is it possible (not only for this) to use mmHg for pressure instead of KPA. Mmol/L for electrolytes, but mg/dL for like Hb, blood glucose, etc.

CHANGES.Acute Asthma Exacerbation: Exam clue 2 now says she is sitting forward in the tripod position.
CHANGES.Acute Pericarditis: Destination changed to Admit to ward.
CHANGES.Atrial Flutter: ECG redrawn with bigger flutter waves and smaller T waves. A 4:1 version (flutter4) is added to the Reading room.
CHANGES.Community-Acquired Pneumonia: No change: rust-coloured sputum is the classic pneumococcal sign. The TB case has blood in the sputum after three months, night sweats and weight loss, so the two stay distinct.
CHANGES.Ischaemic Stroke: Now randomly left- or right-sided. The right-hemisphere version has left weakness, left-sided neglect and gaze deviation instead of aphasia, with a right MCA occlusion.
CHANGES.Pulmonary Embolism: Destination changed to Admit to ICU.
CHANGES.Scaphoid Fracture: Treatment now says orthopaedic (fracture clinic) follow-up.
CHANGES.Severe Pre-eclampsia: Destination changed to Admit to ICU.
CHANGES.Supraventricular Tachycardia: Destination changed to Admit to ward.
CHANGES.Transient Ischaemic Attack: Imaging clue 3 added: MRI with MR angiography confirming the carotid narrowing.
CHANGES.Unstable Angina: No change needed: the destination was already Admit to ward.
CHANGES.Hypertensive Emergency: No change: the destination is already ICU, and the teaching point warns that lowering the pressure too fast causes strokes.
CHANGES.Tension Pneumothorax: Destination changed to Admit to ICU.
CHANGES.Crush Syndrome: Imaging clue 1 (ECG: peaked T waves) now shows the hyperkalaemia ECG as a picture.
CHANGES.Neonatal Hypoglycaemia: New case for the Neonatology standard (hypoglycaemia).
CHANGES.Neonatal Hypothermia: New case for the Neonatology standard (hypothermia).
CHANGES.Hypoxic-Ischaemic Encephalopathy: New case for the Neonatology standard (seizures in a newborn).
CHANGES.antstemi: Redrawn: the ST segment now lifts from the J point in V2–V3, with smaller S waves, instead of riding up the R wave.
CHANGES.hyperk: Severe form added as a new picture: the sine-wave pattern (sinewave).
CHANGES.wellens: Answer renamed Wellens type B. Type A (biphasic T waves in V2–V3) added as a new picture (wellensA).
CHANGES.s1q3t3: Redrawn with a deeper S wave in lead I and a deeper Q wave in lead III.
CHANGES.flutter: Redrawn with bigger flutter waves and smaller T waves, so the sawtooth shows between complexes at 2:1. A 4:1 version is added (flutter4).
CHANGES.hypok: Rate slowed to 66, so each beat now reads P, QRS, T, U, then the next P, with the P wave clear of the U wave.
CHANGES.dka: Every blood gas and lab panel now uses mmHg for pressures and mg/dL for glucose, BUN, creatinine, CSF protein and urate; electrolytes stay in mmol/L. Every case clue was converted the same way (Hb and albumin in g/dL, bilirubin and creatinine in mg/dL).
CHANGES.sinewave: New picture: severe hyperkalaemia with a sine-wave pattern.
CHANGES.flutter4: New picture: atrial flutter with 4:1 block.
